item.text: South Australia’s Independent Commission Against Corruption surveyed public officers about perceived corruption risks, decision making and reporting wrongdoing.
item.support: The Commission uses Public Integrity Surveys to better understand public officers’ perceptions of corruption and other improper conduct.

item.text: It analysed 7,060 usable responses and cautioned that the voluntary sample was unlikely to represent all public officers.
item.support: The responses are unlikely to be representative of all public officers.

item.text: The Commission reported that favouritism in employment remained the leading perceived corruption risk, followed by misuse of authority.
item.support: Favouritism in recruitment and other career opportunities continues to be seen as the greatest corruption risk facing the public sector.

item.text: It found that respondents were less likely to have received training about corruption risks specific to their roles than in the previous survey.
item.support: participants overall are less likely to have received internal training on corruption risks specific to their role.

item.text: The Commission called for transparent decisions and leadership that makes staff feel safe when reporting suspected wrongdoing.
item.support: Senior leaders must support their staff to feel safe from retaliation if they report.

item.quote: Senior leaders must support their staff to feel safe from retaliation if they report.
